key_insight: Running Error Analysis can track finite-element roundoff error automatically inside compiled kernels, exposing instability as computations happen.
engineering_relevance: This makes FEM assembly more trustworthy for ill-conditioned, reduced-precision, and debugging-critical solid mechanics workflows.
method: Wrap generated FEniCS/FFCx kernels in a C++ type that carries both value and forward error estimate.
Compute the error estimate concurrently with the numerical result during kernel evaluation.
Use the estimates to flag cancellation and roundoff sensitivity in problematic PDE assemblies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two demonstrations—Neo-Hooke hyperelastic assembly and a near-degenerate Laplace operator case—and says the implementation typically adds only 2-4x overhead.
watch_item: The approach adds runtime overhead and depends on templated custom arithmetic support in the kernel generation pipeline.
paper_title: Running error bounds in finite element kernels
